blocks.title: One gateway for every model you already pay for
blocks.description: Magpie runs one local gateway in front of every provider you have configured — subscription, API key or local runtime. This plugin connects that gateway to Astravia so its models appear next to the built-in ones.

items.title: Your real catalog, not a guess
items.description: The panel reads /v1/models from the gateway, so what you see is what magpie can serve right now — with provider, context window, image input and reasoning support.

items.title: One click into the model picker
items.description: Publishing writes the catalog into Astravia's own model registry as an OpenAI-compatible provider. Nothing is written until you press the button, and removing it is one press too.

items.title: Agent tools that read the gateway
items.description: Two read-only tools, magpie_status and magpie_models, let the assistant check whether the gateway is up and which models exist instead of answering from memory.

items.title: Keys stay in magpie
items.description: Your provider credentials live in magpie's own configuration on this computer. The plugin never shows them and never stores them.

items.title: It installs magpie for you
items.description: No terminal and no manual download: the panel reads the official release feed, verifies the published SHA-256, installs `~/.local/bin/magpie` and starts the gateway as a child process of the plugin. If your system has no `sh`, or you decline the permission, it says so and offers the official installer instead.

items.title: Open Magpie Gateway and press Install and start
items.description: If magpie is not on this computer yet, the panel fetches the official build (about 70 MB), checks the checksum published in the release feed, installs it as `~/.local/bin/magpie` and starts the gateway. Nothing to type, no sudo. If magpie is already somewhere on your PATH, it starts that copy instead of downloading. Astravia asks you once to allow the `sh` command for this plugin.

items.title: Add at least one provider in magpie
items.description: The gateway only serves what magpie itself has configured. Use the panel's Open magpie button for that page — that is where the models come from.

items.title: Press Publish models to Astravia
items.description: The panel confirms the version and shows the catalog. Publishing adds those models to your model picker; the button next to it removes them again.

blocks.content: The gateway this plugin starts is a child process: it stops when Astravia quits, and it leaves no service behind. For a gateway that survives a reboot, install magpie's own service once with `magpie daemon install`. Without a gateway the panel cannot read a catalog — it says which of refused, timed out, not magpie and HTTP error happened.
